Let me analyze this conflict.

The register says: "R049/2003-NL1-2012.04"
The document says: "R49-1/2003-NL1-12.04"

The certificate ID in the register is 3087, and the source PDF is "r049-2003-nl1-2012-04.pdf", num in document context comment is "R049/2003-NL1-2012.04". The document's own text says "OIML Certificate N° R49-1/2003-NL1-12.04".

Let's parse:
- Register: R049/2003-NL1-2012.04
  - R049 (recommendation R49, with leading zero padding), /2003 (revision year of the recommendation), NL1 (issuer NL1 = Netherlands NMi), 2012.04 (issuing year 2012, serial .04)
- Document: R49-1/2003-NL1-12.04
  - R49-1 (recommendation R49 part 1 — R49-1 is "Metrological requirements for continuous totalizing automatic weighing instruments (belt weighers)"? Actually R49 is water meters? No — OIML R49 is "Water meters for cold potable water"? Let me recall. R49 is for water meters... Actually OIML R 49 is "Water meters intended for the metering of water"? Hmm, R49-1 is about water meters? Let me think: OIML R 49 Water meters for cold potable water and hot water — Part 1: Metrological and technical requirements. Yes, R49 is water meters. The "R49-1" indicates Part 1 of R49.)

So "R049" vs "R49-1": The register has padded "R049" (zero-padding) and omits the "-1" part suffix; the document has "R49-1" with part number. The "2003" revision year matches in both. NL1 matches. "2012.04" vs "12.04": year abbreviated (12 = 2012), serial .04 matches.

Are these the same certificate? The register num is "R049/2003-NL1-2012.04" and document is "R49-1/2003-NL1-12.04". Same issuing body (NL1), same revision year 2003, same serial .04, same year (2012 vs 12). The difference: zero padding "R049" vs "R49", and the register omits "-1" part suffix while document includes it.

Hmm, this is the classic canonical vs printed form issue. The rules say: "Number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate = same-entity with the register's canonical form."

Is the part suffix "-1" a substantive difference? The register's own source filename is "r049-2003-nl1-2012-04.pdf" — the register's canonical form. The document embeds the part number R49-1. This is the same certificate; the register uses a canonicalized numbering scheme where R049 covers the family. The document's "R49-1" is the official printed certificate number with the part designation.

Given the rules, this is clearly a number format difference denoting the same certificate — same revision year (2003), same issuer (NL1), same year/serial (2012.04 / 12.04). The best_value should be the register's canonical form per the rule.

But wait — is there a possibility of different-entity? Could R49-1/2003-NL1-12.04 be a different certificate than R049/2003-NL1-2012.04? The register id 3087 matches the cert_id comment 3087, the source_pdf is r049-2003-nl1-2012-04.pdf, and the applicant/issuer/year all match. So same certificate. The document's printed number includes the part suffix "-1" while the register drops it, and pads R to R049. Format drift.

Verdict: same-entity, best_value = register's "R049/2003-NL1-2012.04".

One could argue the document is the legal instrument and should carry "R49-1/2003-NL1-12.04" — but the rule explicitly says number/year format differences that clearly denote the same certificate get the register's canonical form. The different-entity rule is for company/person names, not certificate numbers. So same-entity with register value.

{"axes": [{"axis": "num", "verdict": "same-entity", "best_value": "R049/2003-NL1-2012.04", "why": "Both denote certificate #04 issued by NL1 under R49 (2003) in 2012 (12 = 2012); only zero-padding and the part suffix differ, so this is a formatting variant of the same certificate and the register's canonical form wins."}]}
